source_text: Nam et ludam inter apostolos Dominus elegit, et tamen Dominum ludas postmodum tradidit. non tamen idcirco apostolorum firmitas et fides cecidit, quia proditor ludas ab eorum societate defecit. sic et hic non statim confessorum sanctitas et dignitas conminuta est, quia quorundam fides fracta est. beatus apostolus loquitur in epistula sua dicens: quid enim si exciderunt a fide quidam illorum, numquid infidelitas illorum fidem Dei euacuauit? absit: est enim Deus uerax, omnis autem homo mendax. stat confessorum pars maior et melior in fidei suae robore et in legis ac disciplinae dominicae ueritate, nec ab ecclesiae pace discedunt qui se in ecclesia gratiam consecutos de Dei dignatione meminerunt, adque hoc ipso ampliorem consecuntur fidei suae laudem, quod ab eorum perfidia segregati qui iuncti confessionis consortio fuerunt a contagio criminis recesserunt: uero inluminati euangelii lumine, pura et candida Domini luce radiati tam sunt in conseruanda Christi pace laudabiles quam fuerunt in diaboli congressione uictores.
thought_title: The fall of some does not destroy the steadfast
orientation: Cyprian is addressing the faithful about confessors who have fallen away, arguing that the defection of some does not undermine the holiness of those who remain in the Church.
pass_a_gloss: For also Judas among [the] apostles [the] Lord chose, and yet [the] Lord Judas afterwards betrayed. not however for that reason [the] apostles' firmness and faith fell, because [the] traitor Judas from their company departed. so also here not immediately [the] confessors' holiness and dignity was diminished, because of certain ones [the] faith was broken. [the] blessed apostle speaks in his epistle saying: what indeed if they fell away from [the] faith certain of them, [surely] not [the] unbelief of them [the] faith of God has emptied? far [be it]: for is God true, but every man [a] liar. stands [the] confessors' part greater and better in [the] faith of their strength and in [the] law and discipline of [the] Lord's truth, nor from [the] church's peace depart [those] who themselves in [the] church grace [to have] obtained from God's regard remember, and by this very [thing] greater they obtain [the] faith of their praise, that from their faithlessness [being] separated who [were] joined [to the] confession's fellowship [were] from [the] contagion of [the] crime they withdrew: [being] truly illuminated [by the] gospel's light, [by the] pure and bright [of the] Lord light [being] shone upon so are in preserving Christ's peace praiseworthy as they were in [the] devil's conflict victors.

choices.why: Keeps the two nouns distinct as in the source, preserving the paired quality of the apostles' steadfastness.
Renders the passive perfect of comminuo literally, showing the holiness was not broken down or lessened.
Standard literal rendering of the strong denial, matching the force of the Latin optative.
Preserves the comparative adjectives and the partitive sense of the confessors as a group.
Keeps the metaphor of disease spreading from the faithless, matching the source's vivid language.

pass_b_english: For the Lord also chose Judas among the apostles, and yet Judas afterward betrayed the Lord. But the firmness and faith of the apostles did not fall for that reason, because the traitor Judas withdrew from their company. So here too the holiness and dignity of confessors was not immediately diminished, because the faith of some was broken. The blessed apostle speaks in his letter, saying: "What then if some of them fell away from faith? Does their unfaithfulness nullify the faithfulness of God? Far from it. For God is true, but every man is a liar" (Romans 3:3-4). The greater and better part of the confessors stands firm in the strength of their faith and in the truth of the Lord's law and discipline, and those who remember that they obtained grace in the Church by God's favor do not depart from the Church's peace. By this very thing they obtain greater praise for their faith, because they have been separated from the faithlessness of those who were joined with them in the fellowship of confession, and have withdrawn from the contagion of the crime. Truly enlightened by the light of the gospel, radiant with the pure and bright light of the Lord, they are as praiseworthy in preserving the peace of Christ as they were victorious in the contest with the devil.

problems.quote: Does their faithlessness make void the faith of God?
problems.source_quote: numquid infidelitas illorum fidem Dei euacuauit
problems.why: Paul's rhetorical question asks if human unfaithfulness nullifies God's faithfulness/fidelity, not 'faith of God'.
problems.fix: Does their unfaithfulness nullify the faithfulness of God?
problems.ruling: fidem Dei means God's faithfulness/fidelity, not 'faith of God'; mistranslates Paul's meaning.

edits.old: Does their faithlessness make void the faith of God?
edits.new: Does their unfaithfulness nullify the faithfulness of God?

fixed: Changed 'Does their faithlessness make void the faith of God?' to 'Does their unfaithfulness nullify the faithfulness of God?' because the source 'infidelitas illorum fidem Dei euacuauit' contrasts human unfaithfulness with God's faithfulness, not 'the faith of God' as a body of belief.

last_rejected.quote: because they have been separated from
last_rejected.why: English passive 'have been separated' obscures active self-separation; they separated themselves.
last_rejected.fix: because they separated themselves from the faithlessness of those
last_rejected.ruling: segregati is a participle; passive 'separated' is within normal range. No meaning lost; reader not misled.
